Kelvin has to discover the correct pad at each position in turn. Every wrong guess costs him a trip back to the start, and he can use elimination to avoid guessing when only one candidate remains.

**Finding position k (k = 1, …, 9).** There are 10 − k + 1 candidates for the k-th pad. In the worst case he tries 10 − k wrong ones before the right one. Each wrong try costs k hops: k − 1 hops to reach position k along the known correct path, plus 1 hop onto the wrong pad. So the worst-case cost of wrong tries at position k is k(10 − k).

**Position 10.** Only one pad is left, so no wrong tries are needed.

**Total wasted hops:**
Σ_{k=1}^{9} k(10 − k) = 10·45 − 285 = 165.

**Final successful run.** This takes 10 hops over the pads plus 1 hop to the far bank, which is 11 hops.

**Total:** 165 + 11 = 176.

ANSWER: 176
